memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Moses listened to his father-in-law and did everything he said. He chose capable
men from all Israel and made them leaders of the people, officials over
thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens." - Ex 18:24-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"Moses listened."

Two words, and they say a great deal about the man. Numbers 12:3 calls Moses the
most humble person on earth, and here is what that humility looked like in
practice.

Consider what he might have said instead. He had spoken with God from a burning
bush. He had confronted an emperor. He had seen a sea divide. Jethro was a
Midianite priest with no experience of leading a nation and no direct word from
God on the matter.

Moses could easily have dismissed the advice on the grounds of who it came from.
Many of us do exactly that. We weigh counsel by the standing of the person
offering it rather than by whether it is true.

Notice also that he acted quickly. He listened and "did everything he said."
There is no long delay, no committee, no face-saving delay to make it look like
his own idea.

Wisdom is not diminished by its source. Proverbs says, "Listen to advice and
accept discipline, and at the end you will be counted among the wise" (Prov
19:20).

The great leader in this chapter is the one who took advice.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Whose advice do you dismiss because of who they are?
2. When you receive good counsel, how long do you take to act on it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, give me ears that hear wisdom wherever it comes from, and the humility
to act on it. Amen.
